_doc: Machine-readable twin of Ink_Painting_System.md. Paint every batch from these templates as they stand; when an owner note changes a rule, change the system doc and this file together.

T-D.text: Traditional Chinese xieyi freehand ink painting on plain warm rice paper: spontaneous, expressive brushwork, each form suggested in a few bold strokes, ink bleeding softly into the paper, dry-brush flicks, large areas of untouched paper. Black-and-grey ink with a single faint wash of {element wash}. {Wide landscape, one-corner composition | Tall portrait | Square}, subject off-centre, most of the paper empty. Subject: {subject}. No people, no text, no calligraphy, no seal, no border.

T-STAGE.text: Minimal Chinese shanshui ink wash painting in the manner of Ni Zan and Ma Yuan, on plain warm rice paper. Most of the paper is left blank (liubai). Level-distance composition: the whole scene is a thin band along the bottom fifth of the paper, made of very few brushstrokes; distant forms are single pale grey washes with no detail, near forms a handful of light strokes, at most one small dark accent. Soft mist separates the planes. Pale diluted ink with a barely visible tint of {element wash}. Tall portrait. Subject: {subject}. No people, no text, no seal, no border.

T-STRIP.text: Minimal Chinese ink wash painting in a tall narrow hanging-scroll format, in the manner of Song album leaves and Ma Yuan, on plain warm rice paper. Few brushstrokes, pale grey ink with darker accents on the main subject, soft mist, generous blank paper around it. The main subject is clear and readable, filling the middle height of the scroll; the right side dissolves into mist and blank paper. A faint {energy wash} on the {energy's thing} and a faint {core wash} on the {stem object}. Subject: {stem object acting the relation with the energy}. The {stem object} is the darkest, most distinct form in the painting. No people, no hands, no text, no seal, no border.
T-STRIP.variety_rule: Owner 2026-11-13 (1 A, 2 A, 3 A): across a stem's five strips the object changes within the archetype's family (the Blade: sword, sabre, dagger, spearhead, cleaver, axe, knife) and so does the composition; the stem's object stays the darkest form. Strips only: D1-D3, the stage and the plate keep the one emblem. Test on the Blade, then the Jewel, Oak and Vine.

T-PAIR.text: Minimal Chinese ink wash painting as a landscape album leaf (3:2), in the manner of Song album leaves and Ma Yuan, on plain warm rice paper. Few brushstrokes, pale grey ink with darker accents on the main subject, soft mist, generous blank paper. The main subject is clear and readable, set slightly left of centre; the edges dissolve into mist and blank paper. A faint {energy wash} on the {energy's thing} and a faint {core wash} on the {stem object}. Subject: {the same scene as the stem's strip, widened}. The {stem object} is the darkest, most distinct form in the painting. No people, no hands, no text, no seal, no border.

T-HERO.text: Minimal Chinese shanshui ink wash painting in the manner of Ma Yuan and Ni Zan, on plain warm rice paper, toned like a pale misty background plate. Landscape 3:2. The subject sits in the upper two thirds; the lower third is mist and blank paper. Few strokes, pale diluted ink, one darker accent, most of the paper blank (liubai). A barely visible {element wash}. Subject: {the energy element's yang or yin image}. No people, no text, no seal, no border.

strip.subject: a simple wooden weapon rack standing on the left, holding three different blades hung one above another: a straight sword, a curved sabre and a short dagger, their edges catching a few small ink-dot glints
strip.subject_v1: two straight jian swords standing upright side by side, leaning together so their edges touch, a few small ink-dot sparks where the steel meets

strip.subject: a large close view of a rough dark spearhead and an unfinished blade blank lying half-buried in a heap of raw ore stones at the mouth of a small hillside mine, one pale seam of ore running through the rocks
strip.subject_v1: a straight jian sword rising point-up out of a misty mountain slope, half still inside the rock as if born from it, a thin pale seam of ore running down from its hilt into the stone

strip.subject: a long blade held by iron tongs in the heart of a roaring forge fire, the whole blade glowing orange-red, tall flames wrapping around it and sparks flying upward, an anvil and hammer waiting at the foot, smoke rising up the scroll
strip.subject_v1: a straight jian sword standing upright in the flames of a small forge fire, the lower blade glowing red-orange as it is shaped, a thin wisp of smoke rising up the scroll
strip.subject_v2: a broad cleaver-shaped blade lying across a blacksmith's anvil, its edge glowing red-orange, a hammer resting beside it, a small forge fire below and behind, a thin wisp of smoke rising up the scroll
strip.emphasis: The glowing blade in the flames is the brightest and most distinct form in the painting; the fire is large and fills the middle of the scroll.

strip.subject: a woodcutter's axe with a long handle sunk deep into an upright log on a chopping block, the log split open around the axe head, a few split pieces and green leaves fallen around it
strip.subject_v1: a clearly drawn straight jian sword with a dark hilt, its blade lodged deep in the trunk of a slender young tree, the trunk split open around the steel, a few leaves falling

strip.subject: a small knife with a dark wooden handle resting edge-down on a wet whetstone at the bank of a stream, clear water running off the blade's edge and falling in drops into the stream, small ripples below
strip.subject_v1: a straight jian sword held point-down above a small stream at dawn, dew gathering along its edge and falling in clear drops from the tip into the water, small ripples below

strip.subject: a small open lacquer jewel box seen close, holding several different jewels: a string of pearls spilling over its edge, a jade ring and one cut faceted gem, tiny ink-dot glints on each
strip.subject_v1: two cut, faceted jewels resting side by side on a fold of plain cloth, leaning together so their facets touch, a few tiny ink-dot glints where they meet
strip.emphasis: The jewels are large, the darkest, most distinct forms in the painting.

strip.subject: a large close view of a cluster of raw pointed crystals growing out of a split rock at the mouth of a small cave, the crystals catching the light
strip.subject_v1: a single cut, faceted jewel half-revealed inside a misty mountain rock face, as if born from the stone, a thin pale seam of ore running down from it into the rock
strip.emphasis: The crystal cluster is large, the darkest, most distinct form in the painting; the landscape is only a hint.

strip.subject: a slender silver hairpin with an ornate flower head held by small tongs over a jeweller's charcoal brazier, the hairpin glowing where the flames touch it, flames and a few sparks rising
strip.subject_v1: a cut, faceted jewel resting in the heart of a small forge flame, its lower facets glowing as the heat works it into shape, a thin wisp of smoke rising up the scroll
strip.emphasis: The hairpin in the flames is large, the most distinct form in the painting.

strip.subject: a small jade-handled engraving knife resting on a block of wood it has just carved with a fine peony pattern, curled wood shavings beside it, a green sprig lying near
strip.subject_v1: a cut, faceted jewel pressed point-first into a slender young green branch, its hard edge scoring a clean cut into the wood, the bark parting around it, a few leaves falling
strip.emphasis: The engraving knife and the carved block are large, the darkest, most distinct forms in the painting.

strip.subject: a single large pearl resting in an open oyster shell on a rock at the edge of a tide pool, clear drops of water falling from the shell into the pool, small ripples below
strip.subject_v1: a cut, faceted jewel suspended above a small stream at dawn, dew gathering on its facets and falling in clear drops from its point into the water, small ripples spreading below
strip.emphasis: The pearl in its shell is large, the most distinct form in the painting.

strip.subject: a dense grove of tall straight tree trunks standing close together on the left, seen from low down, their crowns meeting overhead
strip.subject_v1: two young oaks growing side by side from one root, their trunks leaning together and their branches interlocking, a few leaves
strip.emphasis: The trunks are the darkest, most distinct forms in the painting.

strip.subject: a large close view of an acorn that has split and sprouted a small seedling with two fresh leaves, fine rain falling on it, a small puddle around its roots
strip.subject_v1: a young oak standing at the edge of a quiet stream, its roots reaching down into the water, mist rising off the stream around the trunk
strip.emphasis: The acorn and seedling are large, the darkest, most distinct form in the painting.

strip.subject: a felled tree trunk lying on trestles being squared into a timber beam, a carpenter's frame saw resting in the cut, pale sawdust on the ground below
strip.subject_v1: a young oak with one low branch cleanly cut away, an axe lodged in the trunk at the pale fresh cut, a few wood chips on the ground below
strip.emphasis: The timber and the saw are large, the darkest, most distinct forms in the painting.

strip.subject: the massive gnarled roots at the base of a great old tree wrapping around and cracking open a boulder on a hillside, only the base of the trunk shown
strip.subject_v1: a young oak whose roots grip and split a bank of earth on a hillside, the soil held in place by the web of roots, a small terrace of ground formed beneath it
strip.emphasis: The roots are large, the darkest, most distinct form in the painting.

strip.subject: a tall bonfire of stacked split oak logs burning brightly, large flames rising from the logs, sparks and smoke going up the scroll
strip.subject_v1: a small fire of oak branches burning at the foot of a young oak, a thin column of smoke rising up the scroll past the trunk
strip.emphasis: The burning logs and the flames are large and the most distinct forms in the painting.

strip.subject: wisteria in full bloom hanging in long flower clusters from a bamboo trellis, many twisting stems wound around each other
strip.subject_v1: two climbing vines twining up together around each other on a single bamboo stake, their tendrils interlocking, a few leaves
strip.emphasis: The wisteria is large, the darkest, most distinct form in the painting.

strip.subject: tall reeds and one water lily at the edge of a pond in light rain, the reeds bending, raindrops making rings on the water
strip.subject_v1: a climbing vine trailing down the bank of a quiet stream, its lowest tendrils reaching the water, dew on the leaves, mist rising off the stream
strip.emphasis: The reeds are large, the darkest, most distinct forms in the painting.

strip.subject: a flowering plant in a clay pot with a few stems freshly cut, a pair of iron pruning shears lying beside the pot with the cut stems
strip.subject_v1: a climbing vine trained neatly along a trellis wire, a small pruning knife resting against the stake where a stray tendril has just been cut, the cut end pale, the cut tendril lying below
strip.emphasis: The plant and the shears are large, the darkest, most distinct forms in the painting.

strip.subject: a large close view of tufts of grass and small wildflowers pushing up through cracked dry earth, their roots splitting the crust
strip.subject_v1: a climbing vine spreading over a low stone wall and down a bank of loose earth, its roots and tendrils binding the soil into place
strip.emphasis: The grass and wildflowers are large, the darkest, most distinct forms in the painting.

strip.subject: a stand of tall dry grass with a line of bright fire burning through it, flames leaping from the stalks, smoke rising up the scroll
strip.subject_v1: a small fire of dry vine cuttings burning on the ground at the foot of a living climbing vine on a stake, a thin wisp of smoke rising up the scroll past the leaves
strip.emphasis: The burning grass and flames are large and the most distinct forms in the painting.
